column1: # The gdbstub register NAME -> generic wire register map for aarch64.
# name<TAB>generic<TAB>ground.  This is the SECOND namespace: the spelling
# qemu_plugin_get_registers() hands a plugin, which is the namespace a VALUE
# READ resolves through.  It is not the TCG-global namespace aarch64.tsv
# carries, and the two disagree on real registers -- which is the whole reason
# The names are not chosen here: scripts/cst-regmap.py --namespace gdb reads
# them out of the target's own CORE feature XML and REFUSES to generate if
# this file is short a name or carries one the feature never declares.
# A row whose ground begins "incumbent:" was already adjudicated on the
# Capstone-era per-ISA table, which keyed its value-read route on this same
# gdb (feature, name) pair; those rows carry that adjudication forward
# unchanged so E1's deletion of that table loses nothing.

column1: # The AArch64 SVE register file.  QEMU builds this feature in C rather than
# declaring it in an XML file (target/arm/gdbstub64.c,
# arm_gen_dynamic_svereg_feature) because the register WIDTH is the realized
# CPU's vector length; the NAMES are fixed literals and are read out of that
# builder the same way every other register file is read out of its own
# SVE and the AdvSIMD FPU feature are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE: target/arm/gdbstub.c
# registers the SVE feature INSTEAD of aarch64-fpu.xml when the CPU has SVE,
# "the lower part of each SVE register aliases to the FPU registers so we do
# not need to include both".  So four registers are spelled twice, once by
# each feature, and every one of them keeps the route the incumbent per-ISA
# table gave it -- the AdvSIMD spelling.  That is what makes E1's deletion of
# that table move no published byte.  It also means a value read for these
# four resolves only on a CPU WITHOUT SVE, which is exactly what happened
# before this file carried an SVE row at all.
